output.brief: The slowdown is mostly not Corvane and not the new hires. It comes from one policy change. Credit Policy v14, effective 1 May, requires a full inspection appraisal for property-secured loans above $150k, where the limit used to be $500k. Full appraisals take about 8.6 days at the valuation firm, against about 1.2 days for desktop valuations. Property-secured loans went from about 1.6 to 8 days at the valuation stage. Unsecured loans are back to about 5.9 days, and the firm's turnaround and the Hub's underwriting times haven't changed. Document collection at the branches with new hires is the same as elsewhere. The policy's impact on processing times was 'not assessed'. The policy has a real rationale: an audit found desktop valuations ran 12% high. So don't just reverse it. Take the measured delay and the audit rationale to the credit risk committee and ask whether to amend the valuation clause, for example with a narrower band or faster ordering. Don't withhold Corvane's payment, and don't put the new hires on improvement plans. Add a by-stage view to the dashboard. The withdrawal rise is partly an artefact of the new 30-day auto-close rule. I haven't established how much of it is real abandonment. Confidence is high on the main cause and lower on withdrawals.
